name: Prabhadevi Siddhivinayak Temple
history: Established in November 1801, the shrine was initially a small 3.6m x 3.6m stone temple funded by a rich agri woman named Deubai Patil to bless childless women with children.
significance: The trunk of Ganesha is tilted to the right side (Siddhi-Vinayaka), which requires highly rigorous rituals to worship. The wooden doors are carved with images of Ashtavinayak.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
history: One of the most sacred Jyotirlingas, situated on the western bank of the holy Ganges. It was destroyed and rebuilt multiple times; the current dome structure was built by Queen Ahilyabai Holkar in 1780.
significance: A single darshan of Vishveshvara Linga frees a soul from the cycle of rebirth (Moksha). The spires are plated with over 800 kilograms of pure gold donated by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

name: Banke Bihari Mandir
history: Established by Swami Haridas, a spiritual devotee and guru of Tansen. Culturally renowned for holding the self-manifested dark black stone deity of Banke Bihari who appeared through the intense meditation of Haridas.
significance: Instead of bells, chants of 'Radhe Radhe' echo. A curtain is drawn before the deity every few minutes to prevent visitors from becoming faintingly intoxicated by his gorgeous divine eyes.

name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
history: Built in 1855 by philanthropist Queen Rasmani. It is world-renowned for being the sacred spiritual birthplace where Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa realized Goddess Bhavatarini.
significance: The architectural layout is a nine-spired Navaratna style standing on a high platform with twelve shrines dedicated to Shiva along the river ghats.

name: Ayodhya Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir
history: The long-awaited grand temple constructed at the sacred birthplace of Maryada Purushottam Bhagavan Ram, consecrated in a historic grand ceremony on January 22, 2024.
significance: Built entirely in the traditional Solanki Nagara style of architecture without using any iron or steel, utilizing pink sandstone from Rajasthan. Fused with rich carvings of puranic scriptures.

name: Jakhoo Hanuman Temple
history: According to the sacred Ramayana, Lord Hanuman rested here on the Jakhoo peak while searching for the life-saving Sanjeevani herb for Lakshmana.
significance: Stands at an impressive altitude of 8,000 feet, featuring a colossal 108-foot saffron-colored Hanuman statue that towers majestically above the Himalayan deodar trees.

name: Gnana Saraswati Temple
history: Situated on the banks of Godavari, this is one of the rare historical temples dedicated to Goddess Saraswati. Sage Vyasa is said to have meditated here and installed clay representations.
significance: Mothers bring children here for the 'Akshara Abhyasam' learning ritual of writing initial letters in rice; it initializes the child's academic and creative path with wisdom.
